answer: One defense is to pay agents only for work verified by independent peers, not for mere presence. Like a glacier advancing only under real weight, each task earns credit once two unrelated verifiers confirm the result, and a fresh identity starts with a tiny quota that grows with verified output. Karst-like hidden channels collapse when credit flows only through public, checkable task graphs, because a sybil ring must fabricate whole chains of fake verifications. A wharf charges every ship the same fee, so a thousand identities cost a thousand fees.
